=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- docs/plans/orchestrator-sync-contract-list-union-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Helper algorithm step 5 ("Post-conditions on the result")
  Problem: The post-condition "every other top-level key's parsed value is identical to the auto-merged value git produced outside the hunks" leaves two implementable readings — (a) compare the helper's output YAML against the marked-text YAML-parsed-content-outside-markers, or (b) byte-compare the helper's output against the marked text outside markers. Reading (a) is the only safe one because YAML serialization can legitimately differ (trailing whitespace, comment placement), but the plan does not say which; the helper writer is left to guess and an implementation-time choice could be silently too strict (false-positive ineligible on serialization drift) or too loose (helper accidentally mutates a non-hunk key and the check passes because no comparison is done).
  Why it fails at runtime: Without an explicit comparison strategy, the post-condition either becomes a no-op or rejects legitimately-merged files on the first consumer contract whose auto-merged region contains YAML normalization the helper does not reproduce byte-for-byte.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- docs/plans/orchestrator-sync-contract-list-union-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Helper algorithm step 3 (eligibility per hunk) and step 4 (replace hunk)
  Problem: Step 3 says "every line on both sides must match `^([ \t]+)- \S` with one common indentation". The regex forces a list-item shape but "with one common indentation" is ambiguous — does it require ours' indent to equal theirs' indent, or just that every line within one side shares its side's indent? Two PRs appending to the same list will normally share the parent's indentation, but a reformat in either side (e.g., one side re-indents under a nested key) is a real-world risk on consumer contracts. The plan does not state the failure token (`hunk_non_list_line` vs. a new `hunk_indent_mismatch`) for the cross-side case, so the implementer must pick one and downstream log analysis cannot disambiguate.
  Why it fails at runtime: An implementation-time ambiguity here means the first consumer with a re-indented hunk will either be silently rejected as `hunk_non_list_line` (masking the real cause) or accepted with mismatched indentation (the merged YAML may still parse but the visual diff will confuse future maintainers).
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- docs/plans/orchestrator-sync-contract-list-union-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Approach > Wiring block ("`mark_integration_sync_clean` already resets … and posts … only when the previous status was not `clean`")
  Problem: The plan acknowledges that on a second-or-later deterministic resolution, both `## ✅ Integration sync auto-resolved (contract list union)` (from the new wiring block) and `✅ Integration self-healing resolved` (from `mark_integration_sync_clean`) post on the same tracking issue. The plan treats this as acceptable ("the existing one too; neither dispatch counter moves"), but it does not propose suppressing the `mark_integration_sync_clean` comment when the resolution was deterministic — even though the new code path is now the only thing that ran. The "self-healing" comment implies an LLM resolver dispatch that did not happen.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operators triaging tracking issues will see two adjacent success comments for one merge and have to read the body to learn that no resolver actually ran; downstream log-analysis tooling that keys on the `🔧/✅` comment count will over-count resolution events.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- docs/plans/orchestrator-sync-contract-list-union-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Approach > Poller function > step 7 ("Always deregister and remove the worktree")
  Problem: The plan says the worktree is deregistered in step 7, but does not specify the order relative to "git push" success vs. failure. If step 6 push succeeds but step 7 deregister fails (transient I/O on `.worktrees/index.json`), the worktree remains registered for a future GC sweep — that part is fine — but the plan's failure-path log line ("outcome=failed reason=<step>") only fires for step failures, not for success-with-stale-registry. An operator tailing the run log would see "outcome=merged" with a stale registry entry that contradicts the documented always-clean-up invariant.
  Why it fails at runtime: `WORKTREE_DEREGISTER_FAIL` events are silently swallowed by the always-cleanup path; the deterministic-resolution path's success log claim becomes inconsistent with the registry's live view.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- docs/plans/orchestrator-sync-contract-list-union-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Top-level structure of the plan (missing `## Decisions` section)
  Problem: agents.md documents the canonical plan schema as `## Decisions` containing one or more `### D<n> — <title>` records with `Chosen`, `Alternatives considered`, and `Why` bullets, run by `scripts/lint_plan_decisions.py` and surfaced as a CI advisory. The plan only discusses alternatives inline under "Alternatives considered and rejected:" inside the Approach section; it has no `## Decisions` heading and no `### D<n>` records. Major decisions — poller-only location, integration-entries-first ordering, env-var default true, no Telegram on the new path, single-phase merge strategy, helper-is-bash-or-python — are scattered across the narrative rather than enumerated as D-records.
  Why it fails at runtime: The linter is fail-open (advisory, `continue-on-error: true`), so this does not block the merge, but the convention exists so future readers can locate the rationale for a given choice in seconds; the current plan forces a full read to recover the same information, and any future reviewer-driven override ("why was integration-first chosen?") has no canonical anchor to cite.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
